question: Can a source-free, tokenless, sparse native confidence memory detect when all causal experts make the same wrong edge prediction under shift, beyond strong supervised comparators?
hypothesis: A context-conditioned failure-risk memory trained on synthetic causal worlds reduces the 80%-coverage all-experts-wrong risk by >=15% relative to the strongest nonprivileged global, confidence-only, and fully trained ridge-logistic baselines, with paired 95% bootstrap gain lower bound >0.

predecessor_evidence.note: YNCA-01 negative, heldout already consumed; new disjoint source-free cohort

inputs.name: Procedural latent-confounded binary X to Y SCM; 4 regimes; noisy observed proxy; observational and randomized do samples
inputs.source: Self-generated source-free toy environments, no protected/original scientific datasets, no external knowledge or proprietary models

frozen_design.split: 4096 train worlds from training distribution, 1024 shifted exploratory dev worlds, 2048 separately seeded shifted heldout worlds used exactly once after source freeze; YNCA-01 seeds and outputs not reused.
frozen_design.ordering: Fit each risk predictor on train only; fit no hyperparameters to heldout. Development results may guide a separately labeled future attempt but not retune this one. Each causal expert shares observations and do samples; referee sees expert probabilities and observable metadata only.
frozen_design.data_budget: Each world 90-140 observational tuples and 20-48 randomized intervention outcomes, 3 fixed experts, 4 confounding regimes, no additional data calls or active interventions.
frozen_design.compute_budget: CPU Python 3 stdlib only, 250 deterministic batch logistic steps, 1000 paired bootstrap resamples, <120 seconds development runtime per complete run, no external paid APIs.
frozen_design.capacity: Three fixed contrast experts; native 48-cell context risk memory with 50 pseudo-count global shrinkage; confidence baseline 3 bins; fully trained 6-coefficient logistic baseline ridge lambda 0.05; 80% retained coverage.
frozen_design.evaluator: Fixed evaluator in experiment.py; lower all-experts-wrong selective risk at 80% retention, Brier failure probability, AUROC failure detection, paired bootstrap delta; unknown all-expert failures identified by hidden law only for training labels/scoring.

controls: Fully trained equal-information ridge logistic failure detector
Privileged label oracle for diagnostic ceiling only

classification_rules.supported: DEVELOPMENT_SUPPORTED only if native 80% coverage failure risk <=0.85 times strongest nonprivileged train-fitted comparator AND paired 95% bootstrap interval vs strongest comparator excludes zero in native favor; all leak/provenance and deterministic audits pass. This does not imply scientific qualification.
classification_rules.mixed: Native beats at least one strong comparator on primary metric but not strongest or CI includes zero. DEVELOPMENT_MIXED; no promotion.
classification_rules.negative: Native cannot outperform strongest nonprivileged comparator or violates 15% effect margin: DEVELOPMENT_NO_GO. Preserve unfavorable result without retuning.
classification_rules.invalid: Invalid heldout separation, all-expert label entering inference, missing control or source/provenance discrepancy: INVALID. Infrastructure failures separately classified.

preregistration_note: Preregistration must precede source execution on heldout. Synthetic contributor DEV testing only; do not regard as native model training or scientific first-use qualification.
